methodology_notes.predeclared_sampling: Category lists and pass/partial/fail thresholds for both metrics were fixed before any language-specific evidence was collected, per the Ecosystem spec's predeclared-sampling requirement. The same category sets, evidence sources (official vendor/project documentation, OpenJDK/GraalVM project pages, cloud-vendor SDK documentation), and 0-100 conversion (10 points per category) are intended to be applied unchanged to the other 9 languages evaluated by sibling workers.
methodology_notes.scope_boundary: Only the Java language row is populated in this shard per the assigned-language restriction; the runner is expected to merge this with disjoint-language shards covering the remaining 9 languages under the same rubric.
methodology_notes.snapshot_time: 2026-09-22, single retrieval pass via web search (provider-brokered).

category_findings.note: AWS SDK for Java 2.x, Azure SDK for Java, and Google Cloud Client Libraries for Java are all official, actively maintained first-party SDKs.
Universal JDBC driver ecosystem across essentially all major databases.
Official RabbitMQ Java client and RabbitMQ JMS client are actively maintained with current JDK LTS support.
JDK 25 enhanced the Foreign Function and Memory API (JEP 454), a first-party native interop mechanism.
GraalVM Native Image / AOT compilation is widely adopted in microservices frameworks such as Quarkus, Micronaut, and Helidon, and is supported across major cloud platforms.
OpenTelemetry Java SDK, Micrometer, and Prometheus client libraries are standard, actively maintained integrations.
Java is an officially supported runtime on AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, and Google Cloud Functions.
Maven Central, Gradle, and broad CI/CD tool integration are mature and universal.
gRPC-java, JAX-RS, and GraphQL-java are mature, actively maintained implementations.
Some official server-side SDKs explicitly exclude Android: the Azure SDKs for Java do not provide support for Android.

citations_used.claim: AWS SDK for Java 2.x is the current officially supported branch enabling Java developers to work with AWS services
Azure SDK for Java official service library structure and Java 8+ baseline support
Azure SDK for Java explicitly does not support Android
Google Cloud Client Library for Java is published on GitHub and Maven Central for interacting with individual Google Cloud services
RabbitMQ Java client is an actively maintained official client library
JDK 25 includes enhanced support for the Foreign Function and Memory API (JEP 454)
GraalVM Native Image technology has been widely adopted in microservices frameworks such as Quarkus, Micronaut, and Helidon, and is supported across major cloud platforms

Java.known_limitations_of_proxy: Coverage is assessed via a fixed set of widely-recognized integration domains rather than an exhaustive inventory of every third-party library; presence of an official SDK does not by itself measure integration depth or feature completeness within each cloud/service surface.

rubric.description: Frozen 10-category rubric measuring breadth and reliability of working, actively-maintained external integrations (cloud SDKs, data/messaging systems, native interop, observability, serverless, build/CI ecosystem, API/RPC standards, container/orchestration, enterprise messaging standards, mobile-ecosystem reach), independent of language-level FFI design (scored under Language Quality). Each category worth 10 points; 10 if an official first-party SDK/client exists and is actively maintained, 5 if only community-maintained but widely adopted, 0 if no meaningful integration exists. Applied identically across the assigned language set.

category_findings.note: Official OpenJDK/vendor builds target multiple architectures.
Java is an officially supported Android app-development language, though the Android runtime (ART) differs from the desktop/server HotSpot JVM.
No first-party OpenJDK Wasm target; only third-party/experimental transpilers exist.
Wide vendor support for embedded/ARM/RISC-V/PowerPC configurations via distributions such as Liberica JDK.
GraalVM Native Image produces standalone platform-specific executables for the major desktop/server OS+arch combinations.
OpenJDK/vendor ports extend to Solaris, FreeBSD, OpenIndiana, and OpenVMS.

citations_used.claim: Liberica JDK architecture/OS breadth (x86, ARM 32/64, PowerPC, RISC-V, SPARC, Solaris, Raspbian)
GraalVM native image supported OS/arch combinations (Linux/macOS x86-64+ARM64, Windows x86-64)
Java-to-Wasm is handled by third-party/experimental tools (TeaVM, CheerpJ, JWebAssembly, GraalVM experimental Wasm target), not a first-party OpenJDK target
Oracle is shifting future GraalVM development focus away from the Java release cycle toward non-Java Graal languages, though Native Image for Java remains available via GraalVM Community Edition

Java.known_limitations_of_proxy: This rubric samples a fixed category list rather than an exhaustive platform enumeration; some categories (e.g. mobile, embedded) are scored as binary YES/NO despite internal nuance (e.g. Android's ART runtime vs desktop HotSpot JVM).

rubric.description: Frozen 10-category rubric measuring breadth of officially-supported / de-facto-standard, actively-maintained implemented target platforms for a language's toolchain and runtime, independent of language-level portability design (which is scored under Language Quality). Each category is worth 10 points; a category scores 10 if there is a first-party or de-facto-standard, actively maintained implementation targeting it, 5 if only experimental/third-party/partial support exists, 0 if no meaningful support exists. Total = sum, max 100. Same 10 categories and thresholds applied identically to all 10 languages in this evaluation.
rubric.selection_rule: Categories were fixed before evidence collection as a language-neutral set spanning desktop/server OSes, CPU architectures, mobile, web, embedded, and native-AOT deployment, applied unchanged across the assigned language set.
